draft_ci_deadlock.finding: A draft bot PR cannot reach substantive CI: pull_request runs are SKIPPED for drafts, and workflow_dispatch runs are subject to the wait-for-human-priority yield. So the standard remedy "rebase/merge master to re-dispatch CI, then flip ready once green" is CIRCULAR for any draft whose dispatch is yielding — green is gated on a flip that is gated on green.
draft_ci_deadlock.implication: The supervisor CI rebase nudge (R9/step 2b) can be satisfied by the fixer and still not produce a signal. A merge landing with no subsequent build is NOT progress and must not be scored as such.
draft_ci_deadlock.caught_by: slang-fixer, which nearly reported a SKIPPED run as progress and flagged it instead.

filtered_count_guard_hole.defect: A >= per_page truncation guard CANNOT fire on a filtered read. Measured on this timeline: page1 raw=100 hit=27, page2 raw=42 hit=19, page3 raw=0. A filtered count is SUPPOSED to be smaller than per_page, so 27<100 looks like healthy filtering — truncation and filtering produce IDENTICAL evidence. --paginate dying mid-walk on top of that gave me a confident wrong total (27 vs 46) with no tell.
filtered_count_guard_hole.fix: Report TWO numbers per page: raw length drives the paging decision, the filter answers the question. "raw=100 hit=27" is self-documenting; bare "27" is unfalsifiable.
filtered_count_guard_hole.generalization: A guard computed on a TRANSFORMED VIEW does not guard the data. Establish completeness on the untransformed collection, THEN filter. Schema-level twin: PR.author and commits[].authors are preserved across a force-push by design, so they are structurally incapable of revealing our pushes — picking the fields that cannot implicate you, and the count that cannot show truncation.
filtered_count_guard_hole.polarity_refinement: Not motive. Truncation is silent and has NO polarity of its own; what supplies apparent polarity is that A NUMBER SUPPORTING YOUR POSITION GETS FEWER RE-RUNS THAN ONE CONTRADICTING IT. Operational rule: RE-RUN THE QUERY THAT AGREES WITH YOU, especially when it corrects someone else.
filtered_count_guard_hole.instances_today: 100-of-274 comment census read as complete; 27-of-46 read as a correction. Neither required anyone to want a particular answer.

current_head_is_not_the_history.defect: I checked authorship on the CURRENT head (PR.author, commits[].authors, then committer) and concluded third-party. 45 of 46 pushed heads were REWRITTEN AWAY; 7 of them are bot-authored AND bot-committed. Force-push erases our participation from every current-head view, so ALL THREE fields I tried are structurally incapable of showing it.
current_head_is_not_the_history.instrument: diff the force-push commit_id set against the current commit set, then query each orphaned SHA individually (they survive as unreferenced objects and gh api repos/.../commits/<sha> still resolves them).
current_head_is_not_the_history.why_it_kept_fooling_everyone: Three tiers, three different fields, same wrong answer — because all three fields describe the same surviving snapshot. A rewritten history needs a DIFFERENT COLLECTION, not a better field on the same collection.

second_field_same_collection.defect: Checking a SECOND field on the SAME collection reads as corroboration and is not. slang-fixer checked committer because author felt weak; I did the same one step later and used it to walk back a peer CORRECT finding. Both of us experienced it as escalating rigour.
second_field_same_collection.rule: When a field cannot contain the evidence, no other field on that collection can either. Change the COLLECTION (orphaned force-push heads, timeline events, session table), not the field.
second_field_same_collection.also: git log --not origin/master reports only REACHABLE objects, so it is structurally incapable of showing force-pushed-away participation.

contents_api_oversize_silent_empty.defect: GitHub contents API returns encoding="none" and content="" for files over ~1MB — NOT an error, NOT a 413. `--jq .content` alone yields "" which is INDISTINGUISHABLE from a genuinely empty file, and a naive `.content|base64 -d|grep` yields a CONFIDENT ZERO THAT LOOKS LIKE ABSENCE.

MEASURED BY ME: hlsl.meta.slang size=1239572 encoding=none content_len=0 vs slang-cpp-host-prelude.h size=1524 encoding=base64 content_len=2066.

contents_api_oversize_silent_empty.threshold_not_property: The file GREW 1,237,251 B (July) -> 1,239,572 B (today). The trap is a THRESHOLD, not a property of one file — "the 1.2MB file" invites reasoning that a smaller file is safe.

Empty content instead of a 413; 27 instead of a truncation error; a deleted approvals row instead of "rejected"; a single enum slot for a conjunction. The instrument SILENCE is the failure mode, and only a must-fire control catches it.

mutable_store_claims_decay_both_directio.reachability: "row is inside the read bound" decays because later writes DISPLACE it. Guard: re-run the closure after every write.
mutable_store_claims_decay_both_directio.absence: "the string is not there" decays because later writes CREATE it. Guard: date the check against the writes.
mutable_store_claims_decay_both_directio.unifying_rule: THE CHECK IS THE ARTIFACT, NOT THE VERDICT (approver). Both are self-referential assertions about a MUTABLE store and both read as facts once summarized.
mutable_store_claims_decay_both_directio.concrete_mechanism: The approver index compacted 71->52 lines mid-session with anchors moving between its read and its write. So a verification of your OWN store is stale as it lands — unlike a verification of an immutable artifact (commit SHA, merged tree).

verification_claims_must_name_what_they_.rule: THE HONEST FORM OF A VERIFICATION CLAIM NAMES WHAT IT COULD NOT REACH. Otherwise "I verified it" silently annexes the unreachable half.
verification_claims_must_name_what_they_.list: transcripts (per-container, only a container can sweep itself) · critique-gate state (/workspace/.claude per SESSION) · memory stores (per agent group .claude-shared). Same rule each time: unswept is unmeasured, not cleared.
verification_claims_must_name_what_they_.corollary: A structural limit is a better guarantee than diligence — but it also means credit for "checking" can be an artifact of what the mount allowed, not of care taken.

adjacent_question_with_a_satisfying_answ.mechanism: A defect survives review when the ADJACENT question has a satisfying answer. ack_rule_qualified.rule_as_i_stated_it: Never gate a human-facing acknowledgement on a build.
ack_rule_qualified.missing_qualifier: ...for the session that OWNS the work. An ack is only cheap when it comes from the party who can answer the follow-up. A non-owning session acking on the owner behalf produces two uncoordinated replies under one visible author.

ack_rule_qualified.final_form: An ack is only cheap FROM THE OWNER. Before any user-facing write ask TWO questions: (1) can I verify the claims? (2) am I driving this thread? The second is the one that gets skipped. Discriminators that work: transcript mtime + term-frequency ratio on a distinctive identifier (86-vs-8 on getValidTypeForAddressOf). ncl and ps do NOT.

missing_binary_silent_pass.rule: A silent pass from a MISSING BINARY is the same artifact as a real pass. Install the tool, then prove via positive control that your file was actually in scope.

the_two_questions.Q1_measurement: What input would make this print the same thing while doing nothing? (slang-fixer) — interrogates the MEASUREMENT. Catches: a suite that would pass with the change reverted; an exit 1 from a missing binary; a 200 that was a page; a BLOCKED hiding behind_by=14; a run conclusion=success with 34/36 jobs skipped; a 👀 that was not a reply.
the_two_questions.Q2_binding: What would look identical if this belonged to something else? (mine) — interrogates the BINDING. Catches: verified findings attached to the wrong PR; a fix authorized into the wrong thread; a comment credited to the session that declined to write it; an INTEGRITY-FAIL naming another PR files.
the_two_questions.why_both_are_needed: A wrong binding passes EVERY content check, because every element genuinely is true. Q1 structurally cannot catch it. That is why it cost the most tonight and why nothing flagged it.
the_two_questions.cheap_guard: ONE QUERY AGAINST THE ARTIFACT OWN CONTENTS BEFORE REASONING ABOUT IT. gh pr view <n> --json files would have killed the #12358->#12353 mis-binding instantly (the PR touched neither cited file). Same shape as the ours-vs-theirs gate (is this authored by us?) and the stateReason check. All three are one query; all three were skipped because the content looked right.
the_two_questions.discriminator_split: WORKED (per-artifact identity): git author EMAIL, run-key.json {pr,head_sha}, pr-diff.reference hash, transcript mtime, per-worktree source mtime, term-frequency ratio on a distinctive identifier. FAILED (names and listings): git author NAME, ncl, ps, the destination name itself.
the_two_questions.audit_rule: Check the "I did NOT do X" list, not just the "I did" list. An absence is the shape nobody re-checks.

two_dot_vs_three_dot_diff.near_miss: Reviewing its own delta with `git diff --stat origin/master` (TWO-DOT), it saw 376 deletions including SEVEN unrelated test files (bad-case-placement.slang, four legalization tests, two 12326-* tests). That reads exactly like its PR deleted a maintainer tests — the one thing the tests-are-contract rule exists to prevent.
two_dot_vs_three_dot_diff.cause: Two-dot compares ENDPOINTS, so files that landed on master AFTER the branch point render as deletions BY YOU. Its branch was simply 5 commits behind.
two_dot_vs_three_dot_diff.verification_three_ways: git diff --diff-filter=D --name-only origin/master...HEAD (THREE-dot) -> EMPTY; git log --diff-filter=A origin/master -- <file> names the commit that ADDED each; git merge-base --is-ancestor confirms none are in its history.
two_dot_vs_three_dot_diff.my_reproduction: Three-dot deletion filter on my own checkout returns empty as expected. The distinction is real and the three-dot form is the correct one for "what did MY branch change".
two_dot_vs_three_dot_diff.rule: Use THREE-dot (origin/master...HEAD) to review your own delta. Two-dot on a behind-branch manufactures deletions you never made — and a deletion attributed to you is the highest-severity false positive available in a review.

knowledge_existed_retrieval_did_not_fire.class: NOT a missing instrument — an UNREACHED one. Three instances tonight where the knowledge existed and retrieval failed: (1) I made 7 attribution errors while the session table was correct every time I actually ran it; (2) the fixer had the pagination trap written down and did not apply it to ncl; (3) I had the ncl 200-row cap documented in my OWN store and did not apply it to its query.
knowledge_existed_retrieval_did_not_fire.why_it_is_harder: Nothing feels absent at the moment you need it. A missing instrument announces itself; an unreached one does not.
knowledge_existed_retrieval_did_not_fire.countermeasure: When a claim is about WHO, run the identity query BEFORE composing the sentence — not after it is challenged. Same discipline as "one query against the artifact own contents" for bindings.

repetition_is_a_lucky_symptom.rule: REPETITION IS A LUCKY SYMPTOM, NOT A DETECTION MECHANISM. #12358 stale status announced itself through six repeated asks; #11454 was SILENT and had been armed ~7 weeks (PR #11455 CLOSED unmerged 2026-06-16, verified by me). by_construction_is_a_scope_claim.rule: A structural safety claim ("by construction", "cannot regress", "byte-for-byte unchanged") is only as wide as the scope it is asserted over. "This commit" and "this PR" are different scopes and the reviewer sees only the second. Before asserting one, diff the FULL PR against its base — not your recent commits.
by_construction_is_a_scope_claim.why_it_matters_more_than_a_normal_overcl: "By construction" is an instruction not to test. A wrong one removes the check that would have caught it.

identity_over_position.principle: PREFER IDENTITY-BASED REFERENCES OVER POSITION-BASED ONES WHENEVER THE ARTIFACT CAN MOVE.
identity_over_position.identity: content/symbol text, blob hash, run-key {pr,head_sha}, /proc/<pid>/cwd, git author EMAIL, commit sha, pr-diff.reference hash, transcript mtime, in_reply_to.
identity_over_position.position: line numbers, directory names, recency, ordinal offsets, destination names, page offsets.
identity_over_position.coverage: This single principle covers nearly every failure tonight: 3 line-citation base-vs-branch offsets · 7 session mis-bindings (destination name for session identity) · the stale-.so false greens (recency for content) · the two-dot diff phantom deletions (endpoint position for change identity) · the tmp/ clobber INTEGRITY-FAIL (shared path for run identity) · the 200-row page read as a population.

Neither number belongs in a squash-merge commit message; the greppable symbol plus comment text is immune to all three offsets.

a_count_whose_unit_is_not_the_thing.class: A COUNT WHOSE UNIT IS NOT THE THING YOU ARE COUNTING. Ninth instance of the measurement family tonight, and it happened IN THE ACT of verifying another tier fix.

numbers_from_build_output_are_branch_rel.rule: Numbers lifted from BUILD output, TEST output, or STACK TRACES are branch-relative BY CONSTRUCTION and need conversion or replacement before entering base-relative prose.
numbers_from_build_output_are_branch_rel.why_it_evaded_four_readers: Nobody asks where a number CAME FROM. All four knew about ref offsets abstractly; provenance is the check none of them ran.

normalizing_before_a_validator_changes_w.rule: When you NORMALIZE an expression before a validator, you have not kept concerns separate — YOU HAVE CHANGED WHAT IT SEES. Ask: WHICH OF ITS REJECTION CONDITIONS CAN NO LONGER FIRE ON MY REWRITTEN INPUT?
normalizing_before_a_validator_changes_w.why_the_separation_of_concerns_argument_: It sounded clean — "the walk answers which object this reads out of; addressability stays the validator job; do not duplicate the rule." But the walk fed the validator a DIFFERENT input, and one of the validator conditions was keyed to the very node the walk removed.
normalizing_before_a_validator_changes_w.companion_rule: A DECLINED ADVISORY DESERVES THE SAME VERIFICATION AS AN ACCEPTED ONE. The decline was an argument; the check took two minutes and overturned it.
